  "decisions": [
    {
      "issue": "stack-unnamed",
      "question": "Which language and toolchain should the project use, given that neither the spec nor a repository names one?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Python 3 with pytest, ruff and mypy, as in the stack block. No kstrl.toml or repository was provided, so the stack is proposed, not confirmed.",
      "reason": "Python keeps an injected-clock, dependency-free limiter and its deterministic tests short to write and easy to run.",
      "alternative": "Node.js with TypeScript and Vitest, which would also fit an HTTP ingest service.",
      "component": ""
    },
    {
      "issue": "repository-layout-unspecified",
      "question": "Where should the limiter, config and guard modules and their tests live?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Code goes under src/pulsekit/ with one module per component; tests go under tests/ with one file per module. The guard is framework-agnostic and exposes a plain function.",
      "reason": "A flat package layout keeps each component's allowedPaths exact and lets each check run without knowing the framework.",
      "alternative": "Inventing a web framework and route module, which the spec does not name and no repository confirms.",
      "component": "project-tooling"
    },
    {
      "issue": "api-key-transport-unspecified",
      "question": "How does the guard receive the API key from the request?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The guard takes the key as an opaque string argument; extracting it from the header or field is left to the existing auth layer. Pinned by acceptance criterion US-014 (verbatim key).",
      "reason": "Reading the key is the route's job, and no transport is named, so the limiter should not depend on it.",
      "alternative": "Inventing an X-API-Key header, which the spec does not name.",
      "component": "ingest-guard"
    },
    {
      "issue": "empty-api-key-undefined",
      "question": "What does the limiter do when given an empty API key?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The limiter raises ValueError and changes no state for an empty key. Pinned by acceptance criterion US-011.",
      "reason": "An empty key is a caller bug, and counting it under one shared bucket would reintroduce aggregate limiting.",
      "alternative": "Counting empty keys under a shared bucket, which breaks per-key isolation.",
      "component": "rate-limiter-keyed"
    },
    {
      "issue": "bucket-algorithm-unspecified",
      "question": "Which rate-limiting algorithm meets the sustained rate and burst?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Token bucket: capacity equals burst, refill rate equals sustained divided by 60 tokens per second, a new key starts full, and tokens never exceed capacity.",
      "reason": "A token bucket gives the spec's burst-then-sustained shape exactly, with no double-burst at window edges.",
      "alternative": "A fixed one-minute window, which would admit up to 2 times the sustained rate across a window boundary.",
      "component": "rate-limiter-core"
    },
    {
      "issue": "clock-contract-unspecified",
      "question": "What type and unit does the time argument have, and what happens if time goes backwards?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "Time is a float in seconds from a monotonic source supplied by the caller. If a later call passes an earlier time, elapsed time is clamped to zero. The route edge reads the clock. Pinned by acceptance criterion US-006.",
      "reason": "Clamping keeps a clock step from creating free tokens, and the caller owns the clock so tests stay deterministic.",
      "alternative": "Raising on a backwards step, which would turn a clock adjustment into refused traffic.",
      "component": "rate-limiter-core"
    },
    {
      "issue": "concurrency-unspecified",
      "question": "Must the limiter be safe for concurrent admissions to the same key?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The keyed limiter guards its state with a lock, so concurrent admissions for one key never exceed the budget. Pinned by acceptance criterion US-012.",
      "reason": "Concurrent request handling is the normal case for an ingest route, so a race would silently exceed the limit.",
      "alternative": "Requiring callers to serialise access, which pushes a correctness rule onto every caller.",
      "component": "rate-limiter-keyed"
    },
    {
      "issue": "idle-state-growth-undefined",
      "question": "When is a key's per-key state released?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "A bucket that has refilled to full burst is dropped; the next request on that key is admitted exactly as a fresh key would be. Pinned by acceptance criterion US-013.",
      "reason": "A full bucket behaves identically to a missing one, so dropping it bounds memory without changing any admission result.",
      "alternative": "An LRU cap on the number of tracked keys, which could evict a spent bucket and reset a key's budget early.",
      "component": "rate-limiter-keyed"
    },
    {
      "issue": "retry-after-vs-acceptance",
      "question": "Which rule governs the Retry-After value?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "The functional rule governs: Retry-After is the smallest whole number of seconds not less than the time until the next admission, and never below 1. The acceptance check is tested against that computed value (US-005).",
      "reason": "The functional wording is the more precise statement, and the acceptance criterion is only a lower bound of it.",
      "alternative": "A fixed Retry-After of 1, which would be wrong for slower sustained rates.",
      "component": "rate-limiter-core"
    },
    {
      "issue": "admitted-then-store-failure",
      "question": "Does an admitted request that fails to store still count against the key?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "Yes: the token stays spent and the store error propagates to the caller. Pinned by acceptance criterion US-014.",
      "reason": "Refunding on store failure would let a failing store drive unlimited retries without ever hitting the limit.",
      "alternative": "Refunding the token on store failure.",
      "component": "ingest-guard"
    },
    {
      "issue": "refusal-body-unspecified",
      "question": "What body does the 429 response carry?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "An empty body, with the Retry-After header as the only added header. Pinned by acceptance criterion US-015.",
      "reason": "The spec names only the status and the header, so adding a body would invent a format.",
      "alternative": "A JSON error body, which the spec does not describe.",
      "component": "ingest-guard"
    },
    {
      "issue": "config-source-unspecified",
      "question": "Where and in what format are the limits configured?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "A JSON file whose path is read from the environment variable PULSEKIT_RATE_LIMIT_CONFIG and loaded once at startup. If the variable is unset, the built-in defaults apply with no overrides (US-008).",
      "reason": "A file loaded once at startup meets the spec's 'read at startup' rule without a runtime reload path.",
      "alternative": "Hard-coded constants, which would make per-key overrides a code change.",
      "component": "rate-limit-config"
    },
    {
      "issue": "config-validation-unspecified",
      "question": "What happens to invalid limit values in the configuration?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Startup fails with an error naming the offending key for zero, negative, non-integer or malformed values, and for duplicate override keys (US-009).",
      "reason": "Failing at startup is safer than running with a limit nobody meant.",
      "alternative": "Silently clamping bad values to defaults, which would hide a misconfigured limit.",
      "component": "rate-limit-config"
    },
    {
      "issue": "default-pair-and-partial-override",
      "question": "Are 120 and 30 the default pair, and may an override set only one value?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "120 per minute and burst 30 are the default pair. An override must set both sustained and burst; an override with only one is a startup error (US-008, US-009).",
      "reason": "A partial override would silently inherit one value from the default, which makes the effective limit hard to read.",
      "alternative": "Allowing partial overrides that inherit the other value from the default.",
      "component": "rate-limit-config"
    },
    {
      "issue": "ingest-route-not-wired",
      "question": "Should this run mount the guard in the ingest route?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "No. This run delivers ingest-guard as the function the ingest route must call. The route file is not known, so it is in no allowedPaths. The owner mounts the guard and runs the route-level criteria afterwards.",
      "reason": "Inventing a route file would violate the rule against inventing files, and the guard is independently testable.",
      "alternative": "Adding a route module at an invented path, which would not match the real code.",
      "component": "ingest-guard"
    },
    {
      "issue": "per-process-effective-limit",
      "question": "Is a per-process limit acceptable given that shared state is out of scope?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "The limit is per process, as the spec's non-goal implies. This is recorded as a non-goal requirement (R-11), not as code.",
      "reason": "The spec excludes shared state explicitly, so the per-process result is the specified behaviour, and the owner has accepted it by writing the non-goal.",
      "alternative": "Adding a shared store, which the spec rules out.",
      "component": ""
    }
  ],

{

    "instructions": "PulseKit's limiter is a Python 3 package. Source lives under src/pulsekit/ and tests under tests/; pyproject.toml puts src/ on the pytest import path, so the package is not installed. Run setup once per checkout. Every change must pass the tests, lint and typecheck checks. The limiter must never read the wall clock: callers pass the current time in as a number of seconds.",

      "id": "repository-layout-unspecified",

    {
      "id": "api-key-transport-unspecified",
      "severity": "major",
      "kind": "ambiguity",
      "summary": "The spec does not say where the API key is carried in a request (header name, query parameter, or body).",

    {
      "id": "empty-api-key-undefined",
      "severity": "major",
      "kind": "undefined_failure_mode",
      "summary": "The spec does not say what happens to a request whose API key is missing or empty, nor whether it is counted.",

    {
      "id": "bucket-algorithm-unspecified",
      "severity": "major",
      "kind": "ambiguity",
      "summary": "The spec states a sustained rate and a burst but not the algorithm, so a fixed window and a token bucket would behave differently at window edges.",
      "location": "'Sustained rate: 120 accepted requests per minute per key. Burst: a key that has been idle may spend 30 requests at once.'",

    {
      "id": "clock-contract-unspecified",
      "severity": "major",

      "location": "'The limiter holds no wall-clock reads of its own: the caller passes the current time in.'",

  "decisions": [
    {
      "issue": "stack-unnamed",
      "question": "Which language and toolchain should the project use, given that neither the spec nor a repository names one?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Python 3 with pytest, ruff and mypy, as in the stack block. No kstrl.toml or repository was provided, so the stack is proposed, not confirmed.",
      "reason": "Python keeps an injected-clock, dependency-free limiter and its deterministic tests short to write and easy to run.",
      "alternative": "Node.js with TypeScript and Vitest, which would also fit an HTTP ingest service.",
      "component": ""
    },
    {
      "issue": "repository-layout-unspecified",
      "question": "Where should the limiter, config and guard modules and their tests live?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Code goes under src/pulsekit/ with one module per component; tests go under tests/ with one file per module. The guard is framework-agnostic and exposes a plain function.",
      "reason": "A flat package layout keeps each component's allowedPaths exact and lets each check run without knowing the framework.",
      "alternative": "Inventing a web framework and route module, which the spec does not name and no repository confirms.",
      "component": "project-tooling"
    },
    {
      "issue": "api-key-transport-unspecified",
      "question": "How does the guard receive the API key from the request?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The guard takes the key as an opaque string argument; extracting it from the header or field is left to the existing auth layer. Pinned by acceptance criterion US-014 (verbatim key).",
      "reason": "Reading the key is the route's job, and no transport is named, so the limiter should not depend on it.",
      "alternative": "Inventing an X-API-Key header, which the spec does not name.",
      "component": "ingest-guard"
    },
    {
      "issue": "empty-api-key-undefined",
      "question": "What does the limiter do when given an empty API key?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The limiter raises ValueError and changes no state for an empty key. Pinned by acceptance criterion US-011.",
      "reason": "An empty key is a caller bug, and counting it under one shared bucket would reintroduce aggregate limiting.",
      "alternative": "Counting empty keys under a shared bucket, which breaks per-key isolation.",
      "component": "rate-limiter-keyed"
    },
    {
      "issue": "bucket-algorithm-unspecified",
      "question": "Which rate-limiting algorithm meets the sustained rate and burst?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Token bucket: capacity equals burst, refill rate equals sustained divided by 60 tokens per second, a new key starts full, and tokens never exceed capacity.",
      "reason": "A token bucket gives the spec's burst-then-sustained shape exactly, with no double-burst at window edges.",
      "alternative": "A fixed one-minute window, which would admit up to 2 times the sustained rate across a window boundary.",
      "component": "rate-limiter-core"
    },
    {
      "issue": "clock-contract-unspecified",
      "question": "What type and unit does the time argument have, and what happens if time goes backwards?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "Time is a float in seconds from a monotonic source supplied by the caller. If a later call passes an earlier time, elapsed time is clamped to zero. The route edge reads the clock. Pinned by acceptance criterion US-006.",
      "reason": "Clamping keeps a clock step from creating free tokens, and the caller owns the clock so tests stay deterministic.",
      "alternative": "Raising on a backwards step, which would turn a clock adjustment into refused traffic.",
      "component": "rate-limiter-core"
    },
    {
      "issue": "concurrency-unspecified",
      "question": "Must the limiter be safe for concurrent admissions to the same key?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "The keyed limiter guards its state with a lock, so concurrent admissions for one key never exceed the budget. Pinned by acceptance criterion US-012.",
      "reason": "Concurrent request handling is the normal case for an ingest route, so a race would silently exceed the limit.",
      "alternative": "Requiring callers to serialise access, which pushes a correctness rule onto every caller.",
      "component": "rate-limiter-keyed"
    },
    {
      "issue": "idle-state-growth-undefined",
      "question": "When is a key's per-key state released?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "A bucket that has refilled to full burst is dropped; the next request on that key is admitted exactly as a fresh key would be. Pinned by acceptance criterion US-013.",
      "reason": "A full bucket behaves identically to a missing one, so dropping it bounds memory without changing any admission result.",
      "alternative": "An LRU cap on the number of tracked keys, which could evict a spent bucket and reset a key's budget early.",
      "component": "rate-limiter-keyed"
    },
    {
      "issue": "retry-after-vs-acceptance",
      "question": "Which rule governs the Retry-After value?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "The functional rule governs: Retry-After is the smallest whole number of seconds not less than the time until the next admission, and never below 1. The acceptance check is tested against that computed value (US-005).",
      "reason": "The functional wording is the more precise statement, and the acceptance criterion is only a lower bound of it.",
      "alternative": "A fixed Retry-After of 1, which would be wrong for slower sustained rates.",
      "component": "rate-limiter-core"
    },
    {
      "issue": "admitted-then-store-failure",
      "question": "Does an admitted request that fails to store still count against the key?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "Yes: the token stays spent and the store error propagates to the caller. Pinned by acceptance criterion US-014.",
      "reason": "Refunding on store failure would let a failing store drive unlimited retries without ever hitting the limit.",
      "alternative": "Refunding the token on store failure.",
      "component": "ingest-guard"
    },
    {
      "issue": "refusal-body-unspecified",
      "question": "What body does the 429 response carry?",
      "disposition": "assumed",
      "resolution": "An empty body, with the Retry-After header as the only added header. Pinned by acceptance criterion US-015.",
      "reason": "The spec names only the status and the header, so adding a body would invent a format.",
      "alternative": "A JSON error body, which the spec does not describe.",
      "component": "ingest-guard"
    },
    {
      "issue": "config-source-unspecified",
      "question": "Where and in what format are the limits configured?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "A JSON file whose path is read from the environment variable PULSEKIT_RATE_LIMIT_CONFIG and loaded once at startup. If the variable is unset, the built-in defaults apply with no overrides (US-008).",
      "reason": "A file loaded once at startup meets the spec's 'read at startup' rule without a runtime reload path.",

      "component": "rate-limit-config"
    },

      "issue": "config-validation-unspecified",
      "question": "What happens to invalid limit values in the configuration?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "Startup fails with an error naming the offending key for zero, negative, non-integer or malformed values, and for duplicate override keys (US-009).",
      "reason": "Failing at startup is safer than running with a limit nobody meant.",
      "alternative": "Silently clamping bad values to defaults, which would hide a misconfigured limit.",
      "component": "rate-limit-config"
    },
    {
      "issue": "default-pair-and-partial-override",
      "question": "Are 120 and 30 the default pair, and may an override set only one value?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "120 per minute and burst 30 are the default pair. An override must set both sustained and burst; an override with only one is a startup error (US-008, US-009).",

      "component": "rate-limit-config"
    },
    {
      "issue": "ingest-route-not-wired",
      "question": "Should this run mount the guard in the ingest route?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "No. This run delivers ingest-guard as the function the ingest route must call. The route file is not known, so it is in no allowedPaths. The owner mounts the guard and runs the route-level criteria afterwards.",
      "reason": "Inventing a route file would violate the rule against inventing files, and the guard is independently testable.",
      "alternative": "Adding a route module at an invented path, which would not match the real code.",
      "component": "ingest-guard"
    },
    {
      "issue": "per-process-effective-limit",
      "question": "Is a per-process limit acceptable given that shared state is out of scope?",
      "disposition": "decided",
      "resolution": "The limit is per process, as the spec's non-goal implies. This is recorded as a non-goal requirement (R-11), not as code.",
      "reason": "The spec excludes shared state explicitly, so the per-process result is the specified behaviour, and the owner has accepted it by writing the non-goal.",
      "alternative": "Adding a shared store, which the spec rules out.",
      "component": ""
    }
  ],
  "requirements": [
    {
      "id": "R-1",
      "kind": "requirement",

      "stories": ["US-010", "US-011", "US-012", "US-013"]

      "id": "R-3",

      "statement": "A key that has been idle may spend a burst of 30 requests at once before the sustained rate applies.",

    {
      "id": "R-4",
      "kind": "requirement",
      "statement": "A request over the limit is refused with HTTP 429 and a Retry-After header in whole seconds, rounded up, never 0.",
      "stories": ["US-005", "US-015"]
    },
    {
      "id": "R-5",
      "kind": "requirement",
      "statement": "A refused request is not stored and does not count against its key again.",

    },
    {
      "id": "R-6",
      "kind": "requirement",
      "statement": "Limits are read from configuration at startup, with a default pair and per-key overrides.",
      "stories": ["US-007", "US-008", "US-009"]
    },
    {
      "id": "R-7",
      "kind": "requirement",
      "statement": "A key with a configured override uses the override, and a key with no override gets the default pair.",
      "stories": ["US-007", "US-008"]
    },
    {
      "id": "R-8",
      "kind": "requirement",
      "statement": "The limiter holds no wall-clock reads of its own; the caller passes the current time in.",
      "stories": ["US-006"]

    {
      "id": "R-9",
      "kind": "requirement",

    {
